title: DC-area forecast: Cloudy tonight, then turning sunny and breezy to start a fabulous fall week
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: Overcast as low 60s to near 60 this evening slip to overnight lows in the mid-50s, with patchy fog or mist.

What's next? Clouds clear Monday morning leading to a sunny and breezy day. High pressure stays in control most of the workweek with plenty of sunshine, highs in the 60s and 70s, and cool overnight lows in the 40s to near 50.

Forecast in detail

Tonight: Evening readings fall back through the low 60s and upper 50s. Overcast skies hold on through the night with patchy fog or mist. Lows for most of us bottom out in the low to mid-50s. Confidence: Medium-High

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow (Monday): Clouds should clear from northwest to southeast during the morning. Nice and sunny by late morning into the afternoon. Highs within a few degrees of 70. Breezes from the northwest gust near 20 mph at times. That brings increasingly drier air, dropping dew points through the 50s and possibly into the 40s. Confidence: Medium-High 😎 Nice Day!

Tomorrow night: With clear skies and calming winds, it's the coolest night in quite a while! Lows range through the 40s, coolest north and west of DC. Confidence: Medium-High

A look ahead

It's smooth sailing on Tuesday and Wednesday as high pressure dominates. Plenty of sun and light winds both days, with Tuesday highs in the mid-60s and Wednesday highs in the upper 60s to near 70. Cool nights continue with overnight lows in the 40s to near 50. Confidence: Medium-High

Thursday and Friday look sunny mostly sunny and comfortable as well, with warmer highs back into the 70s. Enjoy! Confidence: Medium

Today’s daily digit — 6/10: Sunday spirits may be dampened by clouds, some mist, and showers in spots. | 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.

DC weather history for October 4

Tropical remnants in 1877 and 1893 brought deluges and flooding to the region, while in 1974 an early-season chill set a record low and widespread frost.
